title: Kanban, Calendar, Timeline and Map show a refused read's raw error instead of the no-access state
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZrgaiMgTJCnswR6jQ

Family close-out of #35317 (PR #36006, Gantt). The #35317 dev found this out of scope. It was read in code only on `origin/main` `98b3f87e`, and no live 403 was measured.

## What happens
When a view's data load fails, four more views print the raw error message:
- `ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx` ~1959: "Error loading kanban data: {error.message}"
- `ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` ~1521: `calendar.loadError` with `message: error.message`
- `ui/packages/plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.tsx` ~1013: "Error loading timeline: {error.message}"
- `ui/packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx` ~1393: "Error: {error.message}"

A reader who can open the page but not read the view's object would therefore see the raw transport string, as the Gantt did before #36006.

## Expected
Each view classifies a failed load with the shared `classifyLoadError` (`@object-ui/react`). A forbidden result draws the shared `DataEmptyState` no-access panel with the existing `list.loadErrorForbiddenTitle` / `list.loadErrorForbiddenMessage` keys, the same pattern as #36006, `ListView` and `RelatedList`. Other failures keep their current error screen.

## Done when
For each of the four views, a pin shows that a 403 draws the no-access state with no raw text, and that a 500 is unchanged (CONTROL). The fix is one PR.
